 'It's a huge challenge against the best team in the league' published at 12:26 BST 12:26 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa boss Unai Emery, speaking to TNT Sports on taking confidence from his side's Champions League win against Viking on Wednesday: "Every game we are playing is giving us more information about how we can get stronger and how we can feel more comfortable collectively and deliver it.
 "The European matches we've played and won were fantastic but now the Premier League is our priority so hope we can use those matches to improve, and show today against the best team is a huge, huge challenge today we have."
 On Man City: "They are a team who play trying to dominate, trying to impose positioning, skills, structure tactically with the ball so we must be so intense in our focus and action individually, duels and recovery playing in our structure. 
 "When we can have the ball, try as well to have momentum, dominating, keeping the ball and trying to stop them and trying to threaten them. It's a huge challenge collectively and individually against the best team in the league."
 On Johan Manzambi: "Each match he's playing with us is experience. It's an opportunity to give us his skills, his good work in his task, he's very important to us tactically how we are collectively thinking.
 "His quality is there, how he is understanding better and better playing matches our structure tactically, his task is very, very important."

 "Bye dear, I'm heading into work."
 "But you don't work Saturdays love?"

 Cherki 'one of best players in Europe' published at 12:18 BST 12:18 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Manchester City spent half of their Champions League match against AEK Athens showboating and Rayan Cherki was at the forefront of that.
 In a comfortable 5-1 win against the Greek side on Tuesday, Cherki showed off his skills in front of a delighted home crowd.
 Former City boss Pep Guardiola expressed his dislike of trickery for the sake of it and Enzo Maresca seemed to agree. But he has also said Cherki is currently "one of the best players in Europe".
 The Frenchman has started this season in impressive fashion for City, scoring six goals and providing two assists in 11 matches so far.
 "I like when the players are happy, 100%," said Maresca. "I also like simple things.
 "The most difficult thing in football is to do the easy things - don't complicate it. Sometimes players that are so good like Rayan, they can do that. In this moment, Rayan is one of the best players in Europe.
 "When he is in the right position - that means when we are able to find him between the lines - he is always dangerous and he has the quality in the box.
 "If we are able to keep him there and find him between the lines and in the right position, he is one of the best players in Europe."
 41 59 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Haaland leading the line published at 12:16 BST 12:16 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 The goals have been flowing for Manchester City, with 23 scored in the past six games – including five against AEK Athens on Tuesday even in the absence of Erling Haaland.
 The Norwegian has recovered from a foot injury and is vying to score in seven successive Premier League appearances for only the second time, and first since 2022 when Villa were among City's opponents. He has, however, since gone four games without a goal against them.
 This season, though, as well as having the most goals (eight), Haaland has had the most shots (27) and shots on target (13) of any player in the Premier League this season, while he ranks second for big chances (12) and touches in the opposition box (40).
 Image source, Getty Images

 'Everywhere we go we get it' published at 12:14 BST 12:14 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Manchester City 
 Manchester City's Elliott Anderson speaking to TNT Sports pre-match: "It's been a brilliant start, seven wins from seven. It's a new group this season."
 On how he has settled in: "My teammates, the togetherness in the group, and the staff have really helped me settle in well."
 On facing Aston Villa: "It's always a tough place to come, they have a lot of threats and we have to focus on our game and how we've prepared earlier in the week."
 On whether City will face a hostile reception today like at Anfield: "Yeah probably, everywhere we go we get it."

 Aston Villa have won four of their last six Premier League games against Manchester City, as many as in their previous 35 against them (D5 L26).
 Manchester City have lost their last two league games against Aston Villa, last losing three in a row between August 1962 and September 1966.

 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Despite impressive back-to-back triumphs at Villa Park in the Champions League, Aston Villa are yet to win at home in the Premier League.
 They have earned just one point from their opening three top-flight fixtures at the ground. Time to change things around?
 Manchester City have lost their last three visits to Villa Park - will that trend continue or are Enzo Maresca's side just too good?

 City sitting pretty published at 12:04 BST 12:04 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Noel Sliney 
BBC Sport 
 The only two previous teams to win their first seven games of the season since the formation of the Premier League both went on to take the title: Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20.
 Regardless of whether any success Manchester City enjoy this season ultimately counts for anything, their form certainly hasn't been adversely affected by the club being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules.
 They are one of only six top-flight teams in Uefa's 55 member nations with a perfect league record so far this season.
 "The mood is very good," said Enzo Maresca, who has become the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a team. "We are happy with our start but we are hungry for more wins."
 35 87 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Time to give Maresca credit? published at 12:02 BST 12:02 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Of course, we know the outcome of Manchester City's breach of Premier League rules is still looming large and therefore we don't know what all of this means or whether it matters.
 But, is it time to give manager Enzo Maresca some credit for his handling of the situation? 
 Whatever your feelings on the situation, it's fair to say the Italian boss has handled it all pretty well. It is no easy task to follow Pep Guardiola but Maresca has fielded questions from the media well, handled the situation admirably and all while producing on the pitch.
 The football has been surprisingly entertaining, given his previous history at Chelsea and Leicester where he was not known for his thrilling style. And City have got a perfect record in the Premier League so far.
 No one could replace Guardiola, but City fans must be pleased with their new man so far.

Football reporter at Villa Park 
 The travelling Manchester City supporters have brought their bananas along with them to the Midlands for this highly-anticipated meeting against Aston Villa.
 It's a miserable day at Villa Park and the City players have been greeted by jeers as they come out to warm up.
 Enzo Maresca has started life at City manager in flawless fashion in the Premier League, can he make is eight wins from eight this lunchtime?
 Image source, Getty Images

 'It's always tough to play against Unai Emery's side' published at 11:54 BST 11:54 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Manchester City 
 Enzo Marseca speaking to TNT Sports pre-match: "I didn't expect to start so well in terms of results, with performance I think we can do better on and off the ball but yes a good start."
 Is he concerned about the ongoing investigation into Man City: "I'm not worried at all because I'm not thinking about it, I don't control it. I'm not worried."
 On not picking Phil Foden despite his hattrick earlier in the week: "The good thing is that because we play so many games we have so many players available and to choose from."
 On having his own impact on the team: "I think if you join this club thinking how good it's been under Pep Guardiola, stay at home. I joined this club to try be myself and just focus on that, we're trying to do our best."
 On the atmosphere at Villa Park: "I think if you're able to control the noise it's nice for the players to be on the pitch during this type of game."
 On facing Unai Emery's side: "Unai is one of the best managers, it's always tough to play against his organised teams. We'll try to be our best. It's a chance for me and any manager to learn things and see things, it's an opportunity to improve."
 42 75 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Maresca sits down with Foden published at 11:51 BST 11:51 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 Another player missing out today, despite seeming to be rediscovering some of the form that saw him win the PFA Player of the Year a couple of seasons ago, is Phil Foden.
 Last season he struggled but Enzo Maresca seems to be getting the best out of him.
 "I have sat down with Phil two or three times, especially at the beginning, to show him how important he is," said Maresca.
 "In the past few years he was not good enough for different reasons. But when you have more players like Phil, you are a better team."
 Whatever the Italian has done, it's working. But if he's to have an impact today it will be from the bench.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Post published at 11:45 BST 11:45 BST 
 Aston Villa v Man City (12:30 BST) 
 No side has had fewer shots on target than Aston Villa in the Premier League this season (22), with their average of 3.1 per game their second-lowest on record (since 2003-04) in a campaign, after 2015-16 (2.9).
 But, having failed to win any of their first four Premier League games this season (D1 L3), Villa have now won two of their last three (D1). 
 However, they are winless in all three home games so far (D1 L2), last having a longer run at the start of a campaign in 2015-16 (9).
